title: Decision: Size limits enforced during streaming before JSON parsing
description:
In kith-tslocal lib.rs, response body limits are enforced during streaming via http_body_util::Limited (lines 210, 302):
  - STATUS_MAX_BYTES = 10 MiB (line 134)
  - WHOIS_MAX_BYTES = 100 KiB (line 142)

Limits are applied BEFORE serde_json::from_slice parses the JSON:
  let body = http_body_util::Limited::new(resp.into_body(), WHOIS_MAX_BYTES)
    .collect().await...

This is correct defensive design:
1. Prevents unbounded memory allocation during streaming
2. Rejects oversized responses before any JSON parsing
3. Accurate sizing: Status includes full peer map (multi-MiB for large tailnets), WhoIs ~1-2 KiB
4. Comments justify limits and warn against raising them without re-evaluation
5. Applied consistently to both Status and WhoIs endpoints

This follows defense-in-depth: size limit is a security boundary.
